items.headline: National Cancer Institute explainer for CSBA: Why and how to apply for SBIR
items.preview: The National Cancer Institute outlines updates to SBIR and STTR funding programs.
items.article:
The SBIR and STTR federal seed funding programs have been updated with important changes that provide new opportunities to applicants. These changes include a new Strategic Breakthrough Program, which can bring up to $30 million to impactful innovations addressing pediatric and rare cancers.
Why this matters: The next application deadline is Jan. 5, making this information crucial for oncology biotechs and any biotech seeking seed funding. The NCI's SBIR Program aims to support innovative cancer research and has demonstrated significant economic returns from past investments.

items.headline: Lanthanum Nanorods Deliver New Drug Candidate That Kills Parasitic Worms
items.preview: A new compound shows potent activity against Trichinella spiralis, the cause of trichinellosis.
items.article:
Researchers at Zagazig University have developed a synthetic triazolopyrimidine compound that effectively kills Trichinella spiralis, a parasitic roundworm. This work combines advanced materials chemistry with biological evaluation, addressing the need for new antiparasitic agents due to resistance and side effects of existing drugs.
Why this matters: The compound demonstrated significant antiparasitic activity, achieving complete mortality in both larval and adult stages of the parasite, indicating its potential as a lead for further drug development.

items.headline: This week in charts: Novo’s rise and fall and AI biotechs’ big haul
items.preview: Novo's stock has plummeted while AI drug discovery startups secure significant funding.
items.article:
Novo Nordisk's stock has seen a dramatic decline from record highs due to increased competition and pricing pressures. Despite efforts to reassure investors with plans for future blockbusters, shares continue to fall. Meanwhile, AI drug discovery startups are thriving, with significant venture capital funding flowing into the sector.
Why this matters: The contrasting fortunes of Novo and AI biotechs highlight the shifting landscape in the pharmaceutical industry, with AI-driven innovations attracting substantial investment even as traditional players face challenges.

items.headline: Endotoxin on Trial: Massive Review Finds Experimental Inflammation Shots Remarkably Safe
items.preview: A review finds that injecting LPS in healthy volunteers is largely safe.
items.article:
A scoping review from Purdue University reveals that intravenous administration of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is generally safe, with serious adverse events being rare. The review analyzed data from nearly 4,000 volunteers and found that while LPS induces a predictable inflammatory response, it is transient and well-tolerated.
Why this matters: This finding supports the continued use of LPS in research on systemic inflammation, providing a reliable model for studying immune responses and drug effects.

items.headline: RNAi drug specialist ADARx raises $446M IPO
items.preview: ADARx Pharmaceuticals successfully prices its IPO and secures additional funding.
items.article:
ADARx Pharmaceuticals has priced its initial public offering at $446.3 million, selling over 26 million shares. The company specializes in RNA interference technology and has received additional investment from AbbVie. Its lead drug, onvuzosiran, is in late-stage testing for hereditary angioedema.
Why this matters: ADARx's successful IPO marks a significant milestone for RNA-focused biotechs, highlighting renewed investor interest in innovative drug development despite broader market challenges.
